summary: This RFC defines a Telnet option for marking the end of a record in data sent over a Telnet connection. It is a proposed standard. Some applications need clear record boundaries in what would otherwise be a plain stream of characters.

eli5.summary: When you read a stream of letters, you need a full stop to know where one sentence ends. This option adds one so the other computer knows where a record stops.

questions: how to mark end of record in telnet
what is the telnet end of record option
what is iac eor in telnet
subtitle: A Telnet option that lets each side mark where a record of data ends.

tldr.problem: Some systems end a unit of data with a special key rather than an ordinary character, and plain Telnet has no standard way to say where such a unit ends.
tldr.mechanism: The END-OF-RECORD option (code 25) is negotiated with WILL, WON'T, DO and DON'T, after which the sender ends each record with the two-octet sequence IAC EOR.
tldr.outcome: Both ends can agree on record boundaries inside a Telnet stream, negotiated separately for each direction.

today: RFC 885 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Mark the End of a Record
sections.content:
Many interactive systems use one of the normal data characters, for example carriage-return, line-feed or escape, to indicate the end of an effective unit of data, called a record. Some systems instead have a special means, such as a special key.

This Telnet option gives a standard way to communicate the end of a data unit. The option is assigned the name END-OF-RECORD and code 25.
sections.eli5: Some computers end a thought by pressing Enter, others have a special button. This gives everybody the same way to say I am done with this piece.

sections.title: Negotiating the Option
sections.content:
The usual Telnet option commands apply. IAC WILL END-OF-RECORD asks permission to begin sending EOR codes, or confirms that the sender now will. IAC DO END-OF-RECORD requests that the data sender start sending EORs, or confirms it is expected to. IAC WON'T and IAC DON'T refuse or demand a stop.

The default is WON'T and DON'T END-OF-RECORD, meaning no EOR is transmitted. Parties will probably use EORs in both directions if at all, but the use must be negotiated independently for each direction.
sections.eli5: One side asks, can I put a full stop after each piece? The other says yes or no, and each direction of talking is settled on its own.

sections.title: How the Option Behaves
sections.content:
When the option is in effect between a sender and a receiver, the sender transmits EORs. The end of a record is indicated by the IAC EOR two-octet sequence, and the code for EOR is 239 (decimal).

When the option is not in effect, a received IAC EOR should be treated as a NOP, though it should not normally be sent. Because EOR marks the end of an effective data unit, Telnet should try to send the data up to and including the EOR code together, for communication efficiency.
sections.eli5: The full stop is two small bytes sent right after the data. If nobody agreed to use it, a stray one is simply ignored.

items.label: WILL
items.desc: Sender asks to begin, or confirms it will begin, transmitting EORs.

items.label: WON'T
items.desc: Sender demands to stop, or refuses to begin, transmitting EORs.

items.label: DO
items.desc: Sender asks the data sender to start transmitting EORs, or confirms it is expected to.

items.label: DON'T
items.desc: Sender demands the receiver stop or not start transmitting EORs.
